minor.issue: Endpoint accepts `target` only as a QUERY parameter and defaults to 100000 when unspecified — a body-only POST silently kicks off a full 100K CH bulk download. Consider requiring target explicitly (no default) or accepting it in the JSON body too for safety.

While a CH bulk phase background task was running, backend hot-reload (WatchFiles) triggered a 'Waiting for background tasks to complete' shutdown that hung the server (~1min 502s until manual supervisorctl restart). Long-running background tasks should be interruptible or run in a dedicated worker to avoid blocking uvicorn reload/shutdown.

rca of the issue: During iter39 test authoring the first version of test_bulk_run_phase_invalid_target sent target=12345 in a JSON BODY. The FastAPI endpoint reads target only from the query string with default 100000, so it ignored the body, defaulted to target=100000 (a VALID phase), and returned 200 with {ok:true, started_target:100000}. This silently kicked off the real CH bulk-phase download (~400MB file → 100K company upserts) that we were explicitly told not to trigger. Immediately after, editing the test file caused uvicorn WatchFiles to attempt reload, which hung waiting for the background bulk task to complete — backend was unresponsive (~1min of 502s) until sudo supervisorctl restart backend. After restart the endpoint was re-tested with target=12345 as a QUERY parameter and correctly returned HTTP 400 'target must be one of [100000, 500000, 1000000, 5000000]'. The buyer corpus grew from 13,172 → 49,853 as a side-effect. Mitigation for main agent: (a) drop the default value on `target` (make it required Query(...)) so an empty POST 422s instead of running; (b) also accept `target` from JSON body for consumer flexibility; (c) add a confirmation modal on the admin UI CH bulk phase buttons; (d) consider moving the bulk task to a separate worker/queue so uvicorn --reload isn't blocked.
